contradictions.fact: Glacier crossing on the standard route (content contamination)

claims.says: Break camp early, cross the Colonial-Neve glacier basin (rope up; it is crevassed with bergschrunds/moats late season) to the base of Pyramid's southeast slopes, then scramble a loose rock-and-snow finger to the summit ridge.
Cross the Colonial-Neve glacier basin toward Pyramid's southeast side.
Break camp early, cross the Colonial-Neve glacier basin (rope up; it is crevassed with bergschrunds/moats late season) to the base of Pyramid's southeast slopes...

Approach crosses the Colonial Glacier basin (crevasses, steep snow finger) - carry ice axe, crampons, and consider a rope for glacier travel; final ridge/summit is a Class 3 rock scramble, typically unroped.
...once the Colonial-Neve glacier crossing firms up but before it gets too bare/crevassed.
...then a long second day crossing the Colonial-Neve glacier basin to the 7,189 ft summit...
N/A - no glacier travel on the standard SE scramble route (unlike some neighboring Colonial Peak routes that cross the Colonial Glacier)
South ridge via Pyramid Lake climbers' path and the Pinnacle-Pyramid saddle; no glacier anywhere in the described geography

contradictions.why: Six fields (itinerary days/schedule/cal/totalNote, timing.sectionBreakdown, rope_note) claim the route crosses the roped, crevassed Colonial-Neve glacier, directly contradicting the route's own seasonal_hazards.crevasses ('N/A - no glacier travel'), obj_haz (no crevasse hazard listed), and the entire overview/beta/approach/descent_text/waypoints/climbing_route, which describe only a south-ridge scramble via Pyramid Lake and the Pinnacle-Pyramid saddle. This reads as copy-pasted content from a different (glaciated) route, e.g. neighboring Colonial Peak, which the route's own text ironically name-checks as the glaciated exception.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The large majority of fields (overview, beta, approach, descent_text, waypoints, climbing_route, obj_haz, seasonal_hazards.crevasses, detailed_rack) agree there is no glacier on this route; itinerary/timing/rope_note are the contaminated outliers.

contradictions.fact: Route aspect/face vs. described side of the mountain

claims.says: E
East Face / Happy Creek drainage
A winter/spring line up Ruby's north side following the Happy Creek drainage...
...continuing up the north-side slopes to the summit.
...continue up the north-side terrain to the summit.
Retrace the ascent down the north-side slopes...
Snow cover typically begins near 2,800 ft; continue up the north-side terrain to the summit.

contradictions.why: aspect and face both state the route is East-facing, but overview, beta, approach, descent_text and pitch_detail (5 separate mentions) all describe it as climbing the mountain's 'north side'/'north-side slopes' — a material difference for a winter/avalanche route where aspect drives loading and stability assessment.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The prose majority (5 fields) consistently says 'north side'; aspect/face ('E'/'East Face', 2 fields) are the likely outliers, though true geographic orientation was not independently verified.

contradictions.why: This is an out-and-back route (same trailhead in/out), so total loss should be close to total gain (6800 ft). The itinerary's own days sum to 6400 ft of loss (300+6100), consistent with that, but the route-level loss_ft field says only 1100 ft — off by roughly 5-6x from both the itinerary sum and the route's own gain_ft.
contradictions.internal_resolution: gain_ft (6800) and the itinerary day-by-day lossFt sum (6400) agree with each other and with the out-and-back geometry; loss_ft (1100) is the outlier.

contradictions.why: The itinerary states the Cyclone Lake camp sits at ~4,800 ft, but the route's own Cyclone Lake waypoint (5,354 ft) and bivy entry (5,442 ft) put it 550-650 ft higher. contradictions.why: The season field ends in July, but seasonal_guidance names August as the single optimal month and September as good — both entirely outside the stated season window. best_season and climate.bySeason.summer independently corroborate a July-September (not May-July) window. A climber reading only 'season: May-Jul' would believe the climbing season is over before the route's own data says the best month (August) even begins.
contradictions.internal_resolution: Four fields (seasonal_guidance, best_season, climate.bySeason.summer, pro_tips) agree the real window runs July-September with August optimal; the season field's 'May-Jul' is the outlier, possibly conflating this with the separate spring ski-mountaineering window mentioned under climate.bySeason.spring.

The current DB trailhead (Thunder Creek Trailhead / Colonial Creek Campground, ~48.6855,-121.0925) is a different, unconnected drainage well north of here and is very likely wrong.

contradictions.why: The trailhead waypoint's own 'note' field flags itself as 'very likely wrong': it describes a Rainy Pass/Bridge Creek Trail/PCT start at milepost ~158 and 4,875 ft, but that same waypoint's 'directions' field, plus road.driveNote and every other waypoint in the route, describe the low-elevation (~1,200 ft) Thunder Creek Trailhead at Colonial Creek Campground, milepost 130 — a completely different location roughly 28 highway miles away. This is exactly the 'wrong trailhead' failure mode that could misdirect a party's whole trip.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The waypoint's own note self-flags as likely wrong, and it is outvoted by its own 'directions' field, road.driveNote, and all downstream waypoints (Skagit Queen Camp, Park Creek Pass, etc.), which consistently describe the Colonial Creek Campground / Thunder Creek Trailhead at MP130, ~1,200 ft.

contradictions.why: The three itinerary days sum to 33.5 mi, but totalNote claims 40-45 mi round trip. Waypoints put the high basin ~22 mi one-way from the trailhead (rib camp distMi 21, summit crux distMi 22.4), implying a ~44-45 mi round trip that matches totalNote, not the day-by-day sum — day 3 in particular ('summit day and full descent to trailhead,' 19 mi) looks too short to cover the ~15+ mi of remaining approach plus the full ~22 mi descent it claims to complete.
contradictions.internal_resolution: totalNote and the waypoint mileages agree on ~40-45 mi round trip; the itinerary day-by-day miles (summing to 33.5) are the outlier, likely undercounting day 3.

contradictions.fact: Rappel count and rope length for the descent

claims.says: Normally downclimbed; at most one optional rappel off fixed slings near the summit back to the north-side ledge. Carry a 60 m rope for it

Most parties downclimb this rather than rappel... If you use it, a single rappel off the east side returns you to the ledge on the north side, and even with a 60 m rope expect to downclimb some class 3 terrain.

...parties typically make two short rappels off fixed slings... to get back down through the ~15-ft crux crack and the exposed, Class 4 ledge just below it. Each rappel is short enough that a single 30m rope is sufficient, though many parties carry a 60m anyway...

contradictions.why: rappels and rappel_count_note both describe at most ONE optional rappel and recommend a 60 m rope (even then some downclimbing remains). descent_text instead describes TWO rappels as typical and says a 30 m rope is sufficient — a materially different rope-length and rappel-count recommendation that a party would use to pack gear.
contradictions.internal_resolution: Two fields (rappels, rappel_count_note) agree on one rappel / 60 m rope; descent_text (two rappels / 30 m) is the outlier.

Summit (7,433 ft)... 'Summit, then rappel off'
Reverse the ascent: down-climb the low 5th-class move and ridge back to the glacier rim, re-cross the Neve and Colonial Glaciers...

contradictions.why: rappels, the summit waypoint note, and the itinerary schedule all describe a standard ~25 ft rappel off a summit flake as part of the descent, but descent_text describes only downclimbing the low 5th-class move and ridge with no rappel mentioned at all — a real discrepancy about whether rappel gear/technique is needed off the summit.
contradictions.internal_resolution: Three fields (rappels, waypoint note, itinerary schedule) agree a rappel is standard; descent_text is the outlier, omitting it.
